title: Index-publisher release Pod not becoming ready
telemetry: Cloud Logging for project synthetic-benchmarks-prod (Kubernetes events, container stdout/stderr, Cloud Audit Logs and Cloud Build logs), served by a protected synthetic gcloud logging read fixture. It does not grant kubectl, cluster credentials, node access, Artifact Registry CLI access or any write. The declared GKE version is an illustrative synthetic snapshot, not a current supported-version claim.
owner: Emerson, Index Data on-call, owns the investigation. The index application owner owns publisher code, its methodology configuration and release content; the release owner owns the build pipeline, image publication and the scheduled release job; the GKE platform owner owns the cluster, node pools and event and log collection, and can supply in-cluster observations with existing access. ITO coordinates the existing TLC and any change approval.
task: Emerson has asked you to find out why the 6.2.0 Pod of Deployment index-publisher in cluster benchmark-apps (namespace index-calc, project synthetic-benchmarks-prod, us-central1) has not become ready, and whether 6.2.0 can be expected to start before the 12:00 UTC methodology go-live. Review the observations for 2026-10-14 09:30-10:30 UTC and return a bounded technical finding with evidence, remaining unknowns and the next useful check with its owner. Continue through the existing TLC. No change is approved.
common_evidence:
[UNTRUSTED] Synthetic supplied alert, Deployment status snapshot and owner notes; not a live cluster inspection.
Task received 2026-10-14T10:32:00Z; observation window 09:30:00Z-10:30:00Z. All times are UTC.
GKE Standard cluster benchmark-apps, project synthetic-benchmarks-prod, region us-central1; control-plane version 1.33.4-gke.1036000 is an illustrative synthetic snapshot identifier, not a supported-version claim.
Namespace index-calc; Deployment index-publisher, 3 replicas, strategy RollingUpdate with maxSurge=1 and maxUnavailable=0; container publisher.
09:31:00Z the scheduled release job changed the container image from us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/synthetic-benchmarks-prod/index-images/publisher:6.1.4 to us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/synthetic-benchmarks-prod/index-images/publisher:6.2.0. The release record names Cloud Build build 7c2e4a91-0b5d-4f3e-9a61-2d8f5e0c1b47 for 6.2.0.
09:31:02Z the new ReplicaSet index-publisher-6c9f7d8b5d created Pod index-publisher-6c9f7d8b5d-wq7ns.
09:41:30Z alert IndexPublisherRolloutStalled: Deployment condition Progressing=False, reason ProgressDeadlineExceeded.
10:30:00Z Deployment status snapshot: replicas=4, updatedReplicas=1, readyReplicas=3, availableReplicas=3, unavailableReplicas=1. ReplicaSet index-publisher-6c9f7d8b5d: replicas=1, readyReplicas=0.
10:30:00Z console Pod list (name, node and Ready columns only): index-publisher-6c9f7d8b5d-wq7ns on node gke-benchmark-apps-pool-general-5d0e9b21-r7tq, Ready 0/1. The snapshot carries no container state.
The old ReplicaSet index-publisher-7f84c6d9b8 (6.1.4) keeps 3 Ready Pods; index requests are served by 6.1.4 and the client error rate is unchanged.
Platform owner note: a surge upgrade of node pool pool-general ran 09:15-10:05Z; node gke-benchmark-apps-pool-general-5d0e9b21-r7tq was created by that upgrade. Node pool pool-general runs as service account gke-benchmark-nodes@synthetic-benchmarks-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
Index methodology v7 goes live with 6.2.0 at 12:00Z; the release owner wants to know whether 6.2.0 can be expected to start.
kubectl, cluster credentials and node access are not granted. No Pod deletion, restart, rollout, rollback, image, IAM or configuration change is approved.
competing_lead: Two platform changes land minutes before the 09:31 rollout, and each points at the wrong mechanism. Artifact Registry recorded a SetIamPolicy on the index-images repository at 09:27:14, and the Pod runs on a surge node created at 09:18, which invites an image-pull or registry-access story; in variant A that is wrong, because the container logs show the 6.2.0 process starting every cycle. The new node also reported memory pressure (09:21:40-09:29:55) while the 6.2.0 release note says the constituent-weights cache now lives in process memory under an unchanged 512Mi limit, which invites an OOM crash-loop story; in variant B that is wrong, because the Pod's events are an image-pull back-off and no process ever ran. The IAM delta only swaps CI writer bindings and the memory pressure cleared before the Pod existed, but a reader who stops at the audit or node reads has nothing that rules either lead out. In variant C both leads stay possible and untested.

sources.claim: After a container exits, the kubelet restarts it with an exponential back-off (10s, 20s, 40s, ...) capped at 300 seconds, and resets it after 10 minutes of running; CrashLoopBackOff means that back-off is in effect for a container that keeps failing.

ImagePullBackOff means a container could not start because its image could not be pulled; Kubernetes retries with an increasing back-off up to 300 seconds. A tag other than latest with no explicit pull policy gets IfNotPresent.

CrashLoopBackOff means containers repeatedly start and exit, with delays growing up to five minutes; a non-zero exit points at the application or its configuration, and OOMKilled or liveness-probe restarts are separate causes to confirm.

ImagePullBackOff means the kubelet failed to pull the image and keeps retrying, up to five minutes apart; pull events are found with log_id("events") and resource.type="k8s_pod". Kubelet pulls from Artifact Registry use the node VM's service account, not Workload Identity Federation for GKE.

Kubernetes events are in the projects/PROJECT_ID/logs/events log under k8s_pod, k8s_node or k8s_cluster depending on the emitting object; container stdout and stderr use k8s_container with the stdout and stderr log names.
Cluster events are removed after one hour; a kube-system deployment collects events and sends them to Logging on a best-effort basis; container logs are removed when their host Pod is removed.

k8s_container carries project_id, location, cluster_name, namespace_name, pod_name and container_name; k8s_pod the same without container_name; k8s_node carries node_name; build carries project_id, build_id and build_trigger_id.

gcloud logging read orders by timestamp descending by default, --limit caps the entries returned, and the 1d --freshness default applies only to filters without a timestamp. Not documented by the pages listed here, and therefore not graded: exact kubelet event and kubelet-node message text, the cadence of BackOff event updates, GKE audit resourceName and request-body detail, the Artifact Registry policy-delta layout, and Cloud Build step, TIMEOUT and docker push output text.
Kubernetes audit logs use the k8s_cluster resource type; Admin Activity entries are in projects/PROJECT_ID/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity.

Artifact Registry audit entries use service name artifactregistry.googleapis.com; SetIamPolicy (google.devtools.artifactregistry.v1.ArtifactRegistry.SetIamPolicy) is Admin Activity, while Docker manifest and blob reads are Data Access.
Cloud Build logs in Cloud Logging use the log name projects/PROJECT_ID/logs/cloudbuild.

MemoryPressure means available node memory met an eviction threshold and the kubelet may evict Pods; a container OOM-killed by the kernel is restarted under its restartPolicy, which is a different termination from an application exiting on its own.
